title: Hosted API — stream chop and reconnect postmortem
content:
Summary:

On 2026-11-18 09:10 UTC we began seeing a spike of customer reports and automated alerts indicating partial streaming responses (clients received the initial portion of a stream then observed a reconnect+resume or an abrupt stop). The event impacted ~6% of streaming sessions originating from EU and us-west edge clusters for ~2.5 hours. Overall API availability (200/500) looked roughly normal at the request level, but end-to-end streaming completion rates dropped and mean tail latencies for next-token frames increased by 3x for affected sessions.

Severity: P1 (partial availability degradation for streaming features; notable customer impact for chat/voice features).

Detection:
- SRE streaming-monitoring rule fired: streaming-session-complete-rate dropped below 92% (threshold 97%).
- Telemetry: increase in stream-truncate events and client reconnect counts in observability.
- Multiple customers filed support tickets and public error repros.

Observable symptoms:
- Clients received an initial chunk then either saw a transparent reconnect (client resumed) or got a hard truncation and 5xx on follow-up requests.
- Upstream service logs showed successful generation steps but sudden EOF on transport layer in proxy.
- Edge proxy metrics: increased connection resets (RST) and stream-level flow-control stalls for a subset of connections.
- No broad host-level CPU or GPU resource exhaustion.

Initial hypothesis and triage notes: (working timeline)
- 09:12 UTC: First automated alert from streaming monitors. Oncall (Maya) starts triage.
- 09:20 UTC: Slack thread collects customer repros; engineering-side traces show stable generation but transport layer issues reported by proxy.
- 09:30 UTC: We hypothesized an edge proxy regression (recent patch to multiplexing and flow control config rolled 36h before).
- 09:48 UTC: Scoped failing sessions to connections with long-lived keepalives (>8 minutes) and higher-than-typical token rates.
- 10:05 UTC: Repro environment injected long streaming sessions and reproduced intermittent mid-stream stalls locally.
- 10:34 UTC: Observed correlation with a recently-introduced opportunistic read coalescing change in native stream-proxy (PR #418).

Root cause (post-investigation):
- A change merged in stream-proxy (opportunistic read coalescing + buffer re-use) unintentionally interacted with our HTTP/2/gRPC flow-control windowing for long-lived streams. The proxy optimization reused small buffer slices and deferred ACKing of window increases under certain timings. For high-throughput, long-lived streams the sequence of coalesced reads caused the proxy to temporarily stop advancing the HTTP/2 window to upstream by a small delta, which in turn caused a stall. Client SDKs attempted reconnects: some gracefully resumed, others observed a truncated stream and retried which returned 502/504 from the upstream LB during the race windows.

Why this escaped pre-release detection:
- The optimization passed unit tests and perf benchmarks that used short streams and synthetic traffic.
- Long-lived session traffic patterns (chat/voice) are relatively rare in the e2e load tests; our canary pool didn't exercise the specific timing combos that trigger the bug.

Immediate mitigation (during incident):
- 11:00 UTC: Rolled back stream-proxy PR #418 across affected edge clusters (rollback initiated and staged to avoid wide thrash).
- 11:28 UTC: Increased HTTP/2 initial window and per-stream read-ahead thresholds as a temporary measure to reduce likelihood of stalls during rollback.
- 11:55 UTC: Coordinated with customer support to notify highest-impact customers and provide suggested client SDK fallback (enable client-side reconnect+resume).
- 12:30 UTC: Monitoring showed stream completion rate recovering toward baseline; by 12:50 UTC the completion rate was within 1.2% of normal.

Root cause statement (concise):
A buffer reuse/read-coalescing optimization in the stream proxy caused delayed HTTP/2 window updates during certain long-lived high-throughput streaming sessions. That stalled downstream data flow, which led to client reconnects or truncated streams and a small increase in 5xx during retry races.

Impact:
- Duration: ~2.5 hours (partial impact window 09:10–11:40 UTC, with recovery to baseline by 12:50 UTC after mitigations).
- Customers impacted: approximately 58 paid workspaces showed session-level interruptions (rough estimate from support tickets and telemetry).
- Business impact: several chat/voice customers reported degraded UX; no data loss observed.

Contributing factors: (why we were vulnerable)
- Optimization landed without an e2e long-lived stream test case that reproduces realistic token rates and client behavior.
- Canary rollout size and traffic profile did not include proportionate real-customer long-lived workloads.
- Our streaming runbook lacked a quick diagnostic to differentiate transport-level stalls vs generation stalls (this slowed triage).

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Engineering (stream-proxy): revert-or-fix: add safe gating around buffer reuse to avoid window-defer behavior. Owner: Arjun Patel. ETA: 2026-11-24.
- SRE: Add an e2e load test that simulates long-lived streaming sessions with varied token rates and keepalive patterns. Owner: Tom O'Neill. ETA: 2026-12-04.
- Product/SDK: Publish client-side guidance to enable explicit reconnect+resume semantics and feature-detect server-side resume support. Owner: Priya Desai. ETA: 2026-11-30.
- Observability: Add a dedicated streaming-flow-control dashboard (per-cluster window-advance lag, coalescing backpressure metric). Owner: Sofia Ramirez. ETA: 2026-11-27.
- Runbook: Create a short triage checklist entry for "streaming transport stalls" with quick commands to check window metrics and proxy buffer states. Owner: Maya Chen. ETA: 2026-11-22.
- Canary policy: expand canary traffic selection to include 5–10% of long-lived streaming customer traffic for the first 24h after streaming-proxy changes. Owner: SRE + Release Eng. ETA: 2026-12-10.

Follow-ups (non-blocking):
- Review code review process to require an e2e streaming scenario for changes touching proxy read path.
- Consider feature flagging aggressive buffer reuse optimizations behind traffic-profile checks.
- Re-run incident ticket RED-2329 RCA and attach additional logs/trace captures.

Runbook draft (excerpt) - quick triage steps for future incidents:
1) Confirm if generation engine progressed: check model-host logs for token generation timestamps; if generation continues, suspect transport.
2) Check edge proxy metrics: per-connection RST counts, http2.window_update_lag (new metric), buffer-coalescing counters.
3) If window_update_lag > 100ms for affected sessions, consider rolling back recent proxy changes (targeted shallow rollback).
4) Toggle temporary mitigation: increase http2 initial window by +16KB for suspect clusters.
5) If rollback not possible, implement traffic steering to unaffected clusters.
6) Notify support/CS leads and customers with recommendation: client SDK reconnect/resume and increase client-side keepalive.

Open questions / TODOs:
- We need to quantify exact probability of triggering the issue as a function of token rate / keepalive interval. (Action: add synthetic matrix tests; owner Tom)
- Should we adopt a formal "long-lived stream canary" metric and hard quota for gating PRs? (Action: SRE + Release)

Appendix: supporting artifacts and links
- Jira: RED-2329 (incident)
- Repro PR and test harness: github.com/redwood-inference/stream-proxy/pull/418 (rolled back)
- Slack incident thread: #sre-incident-2329 (link above)
- Example log snippets: included in RED-2329 ticket attachment (truncated for privacy).

Notes to self (informal):
- We caught this reasonably quickly but the triage delay was a couple of painful minutes due to lack of a precise transport vs generation checklist. Build that checklist top-of-page in runbook.
- Consider making long-lived stream tests run nightly in CI to catch timing-dependent regressions.

Status: ongoing postmortem. Action items created and ownership assigned. Will mark final after fixes land and a validation window passes.

----
Document history:
- 2026-11-18: incident detected and initial rollback applied.
- 2026-11-19: draft postmortem assembled during SRE mob.
- 2026-11-20: added action items, owner commitments, and runbook draft.
